Day 1
From Hotel: 1h 11min → Lake McDonald
1.Lake McDonald
The largest lake in Glacier National Park, stretching 10 miles through the western valleys with dense cedar forests lining the shore. Turquoise waters reflect the surrounding peaks, and pull-offs along the road offer excellent photography angles.

2.Logan Pass
The highest point on Going-to-the-Sun Road at 6,646 feet, sitting directly on the Continental Divide with panoramic views of dozens of glaciated peaks in every direction. The visitor center has exhibits on alpine ecology and serves as the trailhead for Hidden Lake and the Highline Trail.

3.Trail of Cedars
A 1-mile wheelchair-accessible boardwalk loop through old-growth western red cedar forest, descending to Avalanche Gorge where Cedar Creek has carved a narrow canyon with 100-foot walls. Mostly flat, 30 minutes round-trip with cathedral-like canopy and cascading water.

5.Hidden Lake
A 2.7-mile round-trip hike ascending a raised overlook with views into Hidden Lake basin. Mountain goats frequently appear on exposed alpine ridges. Wildflower meadows bloom July through August with pink primrose and glacier lilies against the Continental Divide.

1.Swiftcurrent Lake
A pristine alpine lake in Many Glacier valley surrounded by peaks above 3000 feet and hanging glaciers. Turquoise water reflects Mount Cleveland and Mount Jackson. The historic boathouse offers boat shuttles reducing hiking distances by 2–4 miles.

2.Grinnell Glacier
The flagship Many Glacier hike, climbing over 2,000 feet over 10 miles to a receding glacier at a pristine cirque lake. Route traverses multiple turquoise lakes including Swiftcurrent, Lake Josephine, and Grinnell, with boat shuttles available to reduce the hike to 7.6 miles.

Day 3
From Hotel: 16 min → Running Eagle Falls
1.Running Eagle Falls
A two-level waterfall where flow shifts with snowmelt: early summer brings a full cascade over the cliff face; later, water emerges from a mid-cliff opening as the upper source diverts underground through porous rock, leaving the top dry. The 0.6-mile loop reaches the falls in 15 minutes. Named for a celebrated Blackfeet warrior, the site has interpretive panels on its cultural history.
Open 24/7
~30 min
Two Medicine Road · Glacier
4 min → Two Medicine Lake
2.Two Medicine Lake
A glacier-carved alpine lake set beneath Rising Wolf Mountain and Sinopah Mountain in the quieter southeastern corner of the park. Glacier Park Boat Company runs 1.5-hour narrated tours across the main lake to the Upper Two Medicine landing, giving access to the upper basin without the full hiking distance. The Two Medicine valley sees a fraction of the crowds at Logan Pass or Many Glacier.

3.Scenic Point
A 7.8-mile round-trip ascent gaining 2,238 feet to a bare ridgeline at the edge of the Continental Divide. At the summit the view spans 180 degrees — Glacier's stacked peaks to the west and the Great Plains completely flat to the horizon east. Trail climbs through subalpine fir forest then switchbacks up open terrain to the exposed ridgeline above the Two Medicine valley.

From Hotel: 49 min → Wild Goose Island
1.Wild Goose Island
A tiny forested island anchored in the middle of St. Mary Lake, framed by the park's highest peaks and frequently photographed as one of the defining images of Glacier. The view is from a roadside pullout on Going-to-the-Sun Road with St. Mary Lake stretching in both directions and the island pinned at the center of the composition.

2.Sun Point
A 1.3-mile trail along the rocky north shore of St. Mary Lake reaching a forested peninsula with water visible on three sides. The trail passes the site of the former Going-to-the-Sun Chalets and ends at exposed bedrock above the lake with views across the full length of St. Mary Lake and the Continental Divide peaks rising directly across the water.

3.St. Mary Falls
A 1.7-mile round-trip trail descending to a two-tiered waterfall on Virginia Creek where turquoise glacial meltwater drops into a narrow rock channel. The trail continues an additional 0.6 miles to Virginia Falls, a taller drop with a broad spray zone and a curved rock wall backdrop — worth extending the hike if time allows.

4.Jackson Glacier Overlook
A roadside pullout offering one of the clearest views of a named glacier from the road itself. Jackson Glacier sits in a steep cirque below Mount Jackson, its ice remnant visible as a bright white mass against grey rock faces. Interpretation panels at the overlook document the glacier's retreat with photographs stretching back to the early 1900s.

Day 5
From Hotel: 1h 5min → Highline Trail
1.Highline Trail
A 7.6-mile one-way traverse from Logan Pass along the Garden Wall, following the Continental Divide at 6,600 feet with mountain goats on the slopes. The first 200 yards cross a narrow cliff ledge with a fixed cable, then open into wide alpine meadows. Granite Park Chalet at the far end — a stone 1914 railway hostel accessible only on foot — is the turnaround before the 4.6-mile Loop Trail descent.
Read more
Open 24/7
~6 hr
Logan Pass Visitor Center · Glacier
5 min → Weeping Wall
2.Weeping Wall
A seasonal waterfall on the west side of Going-to-the-Sun Road where snowmelt from Haystack Butte seeps through the cliff face and flows over the road below. The flow peaks in June and early July; by late August it tapers to thin threads. Visitors can pull off and walk under the curtain of water — it soaks anyone who steps close — in the final climb to Logan Pass.

Food Delivery
No delivery apps operate in Glacier National Park. The Glacier Park Lodge dining room serves breakfast and dinner; St. Mary Village and the town of Browning, 25 minutes east, have a small grocery and takeaway options. For a wider selection, Kalispell is an hour west on US-2.
Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted.
Uber is available in the Glacier area including East Glacier, West Glacier, and Whitefish, and is the most practical option for reaching trailheads when the park shuttle is not running. Availability is seasonal and thins out significantly after Labor Day — request early in the morning for popular trailheads. Your existing account works with no local number required.
uber.com
Bolt
Foreign number: accepted.
Bolt has a limited presence in the Flathead Valley and is worth checking as a backup when Uber wait times are long during peak summer weekends. Coverage is spottier than Uber outside of Whitefish and Kalispell, so confirm a driver is available before planning around it. Sign up with any foreign number.
bolt.eu

Many Glacier Trailhead · Glacier

The park's most celebrated glacier hike starts at Many Glacier and climbs past Grinnell Lake and Upper Grinnell Lake to the ice itself. The glacier has retreated dramatically since the 1930s photographs posted along the trail. A boat shuttle from the Many Glacier Hotel dock cuts 3.4 miles from the return; book at the trailhead the morning you go.

A paved-then-boardwalk trail from Logan Pass climbs past wildflower meadows to a ridge above Hidden Lake and its colony of mountain goats. The overlook sits at 7,120 feet. Start before 8:00am or after 4:00pm to walk it in something close to quiet.

Avalanche Campground · Glacier

The trail runs through old-growth cedar and hemlock before climbing beside Avalanche Creek into a glacially carved cirque. The lake sits below four waterfalls fed by Sperry Glacier above; in early summer the meltwater runs continuous. A shaded old-growth section makes this one of the cooler options on a hot July afternoon.

Worth Knowing

The Hotel Lobby Was Built From Trees Too Big to Grow in Montana

The hotel guests check into on this trip is itself a piece of the park's engineering history. The lodge was built in 1913 by the Great Northern Railway to draw passengers to its new rail line, and its three-story lobby is ringed by sixty Douglas-fir columns each roughly 40 feet tall — timber so massive that Montana's own forests couldn't supply it. Every log was cut in the Pacific Northwest during the specific season when sap runs low, so the bark would stay attached during transport, then shipped in by rail on custom-built cars. A crew of about 75 men spent a year and a half raising the frame using nothing but horses, chains, and pulleys — no cranes, no machinery — which is how the building earned its local nickname, the Big Tree Lodge.

The park's namesake ice has been quietly disappearing for over a century. Around 1850, roughly 150 glaciers carved these valleys; today only about 26 are still named and mapped. Signs at the visitor centers once carried a hard target date for when every glacier would vanish entirely, a projection based on early-2000s climate models — but when the melt rate slowed more than expected, the park quietly pulled those signs and replaced them with a vaguer warning that the timeline "depends on how and when we act." The ice is still retreating, just not on the exact scientific timetable the park itself once posted on its own walls.
